detail: Between 5% and 10% below the high counts as a pullback, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 on Wednesday, about 8.1% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October. It was down as much as 3.2% during the day before buyers stepped in, a reminder of how fast moods swing in a nervous market.
source: Reuters closing figures via New Straits Times, 25 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was mixed on Wednesday: on the Nasdaq 2,902 shares rose and 2,009 fell, but 479 hit new 52-week lows against 44 new highs. Most shares held up while big AI and chip names fell, so the damage was concentrated in the largest companies rather than market-wide.
source: Reuters closing breadth via New Straits Times, 25 Nov

detail: Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield eased to about 4.85% on Wednesday as money moved out of tech shares and into bonds. Safe bonds paying close to 5% still set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: Swingfolio US close and Alliance News, 25 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: after hotter US inflation figures, fed funds futures put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 98%, and markets price about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: Fed funds futures via Yahoo Finance, 25 Nov; Bloomberg via FXStreet and RateProbability OIS pricing, 26 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, and Brent crude rose 2.1% to settle at $96.57 on Thursday, a third day of gains, after a Houthi claim of an attack on a Saudi refinery and Iranian reports of tankers hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz. Dearer oil feeds into fuel and transport costs, which can keep inflation and interest rates higher for longer.
source: ICE settlement via Nation Thailand and GSM Global News, 26 Nov
